Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone, then one. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud's results for the third quarter fiscal 2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud had an exceptional third quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. This success is a testament to our innovative technology, dedicated team, and strong customer relationships.

During the quarter, we focused on five key areas:
1. Expanding our market share in key verticals.
2. Investing in cutting-edge research and development.
3. Enhancing our cloud security posture.
4. Driving operational efficiencies.
5. Strengthening our ecosystem partnerships.

Let me elaborate on our efforts to bolster our cloud security posture, which remains a top priority amid escalating cyber threats in the cloud computing landscape. As global cloud spend surpasses $600 billion this year, driven by hyperscale IaaS and PaaS migrations, we've seen ransomware attempts rise 42% year-over-year based on our threat intelligence integrated with reports like Mandiant's M-Trends. Nation-state actors continue probing supply chains, reminiscent of past incidents like SolarWinds.

In Q3, we committed $285 million to security initiatives, up 28% from last year and accounting for 14.2% of total opex, compared to 11.8% previously. This breaks down to $180 million in infrastructure capex, or 63%, and $105 million in personnel costs, or 37%. Year-to-date, we've invested $520 million, on pace for $1.15 billion annually, equating to about 8.5% of our projected 2024 revenue of $13.5 billion. These aren't merely protective measures; they form a competitive moat, fueling 35% quarter-over-quarter growth in financial services workloads and 52% year-over-year bookings in HIPAA-compliant PaaS for healthcare.

On the infrastructure side, we've rolled out our next-generation zero-trust architecture across all 28 global regions, now safeguarding 98% of customer workloads—achieved three quarters ahead of schedule. We allocated $95 million to AI/ML-driven threat detection platforms, enhancing our ForgeSentinel SIEM system—akin to advanced tools in the market—which uses generative AI on 15 petabytes of anonymized data. This slashed mean-time-to-detect for advanced persistent threats to under two minutes, versus the 14-minute industry norm per Gartner. Integrated with endpoint detection like CrowdStrike and behavioral analytics, it thwarted 1.7 million zero-day exploits, cutting incidents by 65% year-over-year per million workloads.

We invested $65 million in confidential computing hardware, including 50,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs with confidential capabilities and AMD SEV-SNP enclaves for bare-metal instances. This meets surging needs for data-in-use protection following vulnerabilities like Log4Shell and MOVEit. Leading banks are deploying homomorphic encryption workloads with zero data exfiltration even in simulated quantum scenarios.

Additionally, $20 million went to expanding our Secure Access Service Edge fabric across 150 edge points of presence, incorporating proxying and secure web gateways. This bolsters hybrid workforces, reducing lateral movement risks by 72% in pentests.

Regionally, EMEA saw a 40% quarter-over-quarter uptick to $72 million, prioritizing NIS2 compliance and sovereignty with three new Frankfurt-adjacent zones featuring EU-only key management—securing €450 million in public sector sovereign deals post-Schrems II. In APAC, $55 million supported ASEAN expansion in Tokyo and Singapore with post-quantum cryptography like Kyber-1024, ahead of Japan's mandates and driving 22% regional revenue growth. U.S. federal investments of $38 million focused on FedRAMP High and CMMC 2.0, landing a $200 million DoD IL5 contract ahead of Azure Government rivals.

For personnel, our security team expanded by 1,200 to 4,800 full-time equivalents, a 33% increase with 7.2-year average tenure. Q3 opex covered $45 million for hiring certified experts from firms like Palo Alto and FireEye, $35 million for upskilling through our Security Academy with SANS, and $25 million for retention amid a 25% talent shortage per ISC². Retention stands at 92% via SLA-tied equity. Our SecOps center processes 450,000 daily alerts with 85% auto-remediation, allowing focus on MITRE ATT&CK simulations.

These efforts deliver clear returns: security NPS at 78 versus industry 62, linking to 15% lower enterprise churn. We've closed 60% of regulated industry proofs-of-concept, surpassing AWS benchmarks. Security opex as a revenue percentage fell to 6.8% from 7.4% through multi-tenant scale efficiencies.

Forward, we're scaling to $1.3 billion in 2025 spend, including $300 million for quantum-safe transitions and GenAI red-teaming, positioning us to dominate the trust-first cloud market where security services grow at 19% CAGR through 2028 per IDC.

Now I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a stellar financial performance in the third quarter. Revenue grew by 32% year-over-year to $29.2 billion, significantly outpacing industry averages. Our gross margin was 73.2%, reflecting our pricing power and efficient cost management. Our operating margin was 32%.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'm excited to highlight our overall financial performance for Q3 and the full fiscal year to date, which demonstrates resilience and momentum in our hyperscale IaaS, PaaS, and AI-optimized cloud platform amid macroeconomic shifts. As a leader in this space, we've achieved record results powered by generative AI demand, data sovereignty, and hybrid multi-cloud needs.

Top line: Q3 revenue hit $7.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, beating guidance by $250 million. Year-to-date, we're at a 32% growth pace from 25% last year, grabbing share in a 22% CAGR market per Gartner, thanks to legacy migrations and LLM adoption.

By segment: Infrastructure Services (IaaS) at $4.9 billion, 35% up, 63% of revenue—consumption soared 42% on GPU instances like our Nexara H100 clusters at 150% utilization. Our Graviton4 ARM instances match custom silicon trends, offering 25% better price-performance for inference.

Platform and Data Services (PaaS/SaaS) reached $2.1 billion, 22% growth, with ARR over $12 billion up 40%. Managed Kubernetes and serverless shine, like zero-ETL data lakes for banks, akin to integrated Snowflake momentum.

Edge and Sovereign Cloud exploded 55% to $800 million, with $2.5 billion multi-year regulated wins mirroring strategic plays.

Profitability: GAAP operating income $2.1 billion at 27% margin, up 400 bps; non-GAAP 32% from 29%. Free cash flow $2.4 billion quarterly, $9.1 billion yearly or 31% of revenue—funding $1.2 billion repurchases and $0.15 dividend start. EBITDA margins at 35% with 120 zones in 35 regions.

Customers: DBNRR 128% from 122%, 70% of top accounts on GenAI. Added 450 logos, including $500 million automotive deal. RPO up 45% to $45 billion, current 52% to $18 billion.

Regions: Americas 65% share, 25% to $5.1 billion on federal wins; EMEA 38% to $1.7 billion on sovereign zones; APAC 42% to $1.0 billion on 5G edge.

Capex $4.5 billion (15% revenue) for AI and green data centers like 1 GW Sweden hydro site. Amid optimizations, our discounts hit 20% attach. AI endpoints target 15% of $200 billion GenAI TAM.

This sets FY24 revenue at $36-37 billion (23-27% growth), op margins 33-34%.

Now, I'll hand it over to Taylor Kim for a technical update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. From a technology perspective, we made significant strides in several key areas this quarter. We are proud to announce the general availability of our new Nexara AI platform, which offers unparalleled performance and scalability.

Today, I'd like to delve into our Cloud Services segment gross margin, which expanded to 73.2%—up 210 basis points year-over-year and 80 sequentially—marking 11 straight quarters of gains. This reflects our profitability engine in hyperscale cloud, aligning with AWS at 72% and ahead of others.

Cloud Services revenue was $18.4 billion, up 28%, 62% of total. Margin factors include data center ops, power, network, D&A, and support.

Key drivers:

Revenue mix shift: +120 bps from high-margin AI/ML at $4.2 billion, 162% growth, 23% mix—82% margins on GPU inference with 2-3x pricing. PaaS at 75%, SaaS over 85%.

Efficiencies: +60 bps, utilization to 92% via AetherOptix orchestration; PUE to 1.18 with 62% renewables, 12% drop; D&A down 150 bps; bandwidth cuts via CDN and cables.

Tech innovations: +40 bps, Neptune ARM Gen3 on 45% fleet, 28% better perf, 40% less power; hypervisor boosts density 20%; confidential enclaves unlock 15% capacity.

Regions: NA 76%, EMEA 74% up 300 bps, APAC 68% ramping, LATAM/ME 70%.

Strategically, sovereign builds, NVIDIA/Intel partnerships, stable ASPs $0.45/core-hour. Q4 guide 73.5-74.0%, FY25 +100-150 bps on AI/utilization. GPU hedges, energy locks mitigate risks.

We're engineering hyperscale profitability.

I'll now pass it to Morgan Patel for a product roadmap update.

Morgan Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. This quarter, we launched Nexara GreenOps, a game-changing solution for energy-sensitive enterprises. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. We are seeing strong demand and a rapid increase in adoption.

Turning to our total revenue for Q3 ended September 30, 2024: $29.8 billion, up 22% year-over-year—our 15th quarter of acceleration—beating $29.0-29.5 billion guidance by $300 million or 1%. This topped IDC's 21% market growth, outrunning AWS 19% and nearing Azure 30% via IaaS/PaaS/SaaS execution.

Core infrastructure $20.3 billion, 68%, 25% up on Graviton4 (40% adoption) and 2.5x GPU ramp for hyperscale training like GPT-scale models.

AI/ML $4.2 billion, 55% surge, 14% share—Bedrock with Claude/Mistral fine-tuning added 12k developers; Trainium2 cuts inference 25%.

Regions: Americas $17.2 billion 24% on FedRAMP/Canada; EMEA $7.1 billion 20% on GDPR zones/SAP; APAC $5.5 billion 28% on sovereignty/NTT ties.

Multi-cloud Outposts +45%, Savings Plans boost NRR 118%. Q4 guide $30.8-31.3 billion, 21-24%, AI 50%+—cloud's OpEx shift targets $1.2T TAM.

Now, back to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Morgan. We are incredibly excited about the future. We believe our investments in innovation, our commitment to customer success, and our talented team will continue to drive strong growth and value creation.

Looking ahead to FY24 close and Q1 FY25, macroeconomic factors shape our guidance. We navigated Q3 resiliently with 28% revenue growth to $22.4 billion, but inflation, high rates, and capex softening loom. Fed rates at 5.25-5.50% extend project paybacks, with 10-15% drop in $10M+ deals like peers—Q4 growth drag 200-300 bps, FY24 24-26% vs prior 26-28%. Cloud ROI (3x faster) favors opex.

Inflation hits energy 25% on AI; PUE 1.18 steady, FY25 OpEx +$450-500M offset by 15% pricing, boosting GreenOps 40% adoption.

FX: Strong USD 8% vs EUR, 12% vs JPY—3-4% headwind on 35% international; hedges and Japan sovereign help.

Regions: NA 55% 30%+ on GenAI (Meta/OpenAI ramps, 2.5x throughput); EMEA 25% 18-20% on ECB/GDPR, EdgeFabric 25% telco; APAC 15% 35%+ on China+1/India, Graviton4 20% TCO; LATAM/ROW 5% 22% on nearshoring.

Capex $12B FY24 (60% AI) for 50 EWAR; Zero-Trust Autoscaler +150 bps margin to 78%; Fabric API for hybrid (62% enterprises per Flexera).

Q4 revenue $23.8-24.2B (25% mid), FY25 22-25%, EPS $2.15-2.20, FCF 90%+. Cloud counter-cyclical, 21% CAGR to 2027.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Alex, on the macro outlook, with rates staying high and capex scrutiny, how do you see the bifurcation by region playing out into FY25, and any adjustments to capex allocation?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. Great question. As I outlined, we're seeing resilience in NA and APAC offsetting EMEA moderation. Our $12 billion capex remains front-loaded on AI capacity to capture GenAI TAM, with levers like Zero-Trust Autoscaler ensuring efficiencies. We're confident in 22-25% FY25 growth through cloud-native resilience and 90% FCF conversion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi team, strong margins again. Jordan, can you expand on the free cash flow drivers and sustainability given capex intensity?

Jordan Lee:
Hi Lisa. Absolutely. Q3 FCF at $2.4 billion reflects 35% EBITDA margins, scale in 120 zones, and 92% utilization. Unit costs down 15% via liquid cooling and renewables at 65%. With RPO visibility and 128% NRR, we expect continued 30%+ FCF margins, supporting repurchases and our new dividend.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Thanks. Taylor, impressive gross margin expansion. What technical innovations give you confidence in 73.5-74% Q4, especially around custom silicon and AI mix?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Mike. Neptune Gen3 ARM powers 45% of fleet for 28% perf gains, paired with hypervisor density boosts and confidential enclaves freeing 15% capacity. AI mix to 30% revenue with 82% margins, plus PUE 1.18 and 95% utilization target—positioned for 100-150 bps FY25 expansion despite GPU risks, which we're hedged on.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your insightful questions and your continued interest in Nexara Cloud. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Cloud services gross margin: factors influencing profitability
Investment in security infrastructure and personnel
Total revenue: actual vs. guidance, YoY growth

aspect_summary.Expected impact of macroeconomic factors: High interest rates (Fed 5.25-5.50%), inflation (25% on energy), and capex softening expected to drag Q4 growth by 200-300 bps and FY24 to 24-26% (vs prior 26-28%), with 10-15% drop in large deals and FX headwinds from strong USD (3-4% impact); cloud resilience, regional strengths (NA/APAC), and pricing offsets support FY25 22-25% growth.
aspect_summary.Overall financial performance highlights: Stellar Q3 with revenue $22.4-29.8B (22-32% YoY growth, beating guidance), 73.2% gross margin, 32% operating margin, $2.4B FCF (31% of revenue), driven by AI demand, IaaS/PaaS growth, high utilization, and RPO up 45% to $45B; FY24 guidance $36-37B (23-27% growth).
aspect_summary.Cloud services gross margin: factors inf: Expanded to 73.2% (+210 bps YoY) from high-margin AI/ML mix shift (+120 bps, 82% margins), operational efficiencies (+60 bps: 92% utilization, PUE 1.18, lower D&A/power), and tech innovations (+40 bps: Neptune ARM Gen3, hypervisor density, confidential enclaves); Q4 guide 73.5-74%, FY25 +100-150 bps.
aspect_summary.Investment in security infrastructure an: Q3 $285M total (up 28% YoY, 14.2% opex): $180M infrastructure (zero-trust across 28 regions, $95M AI/ML threat detection, $65M confidential computing GPUs/enclaves, $20M SASE expansion) and $105M personnel (team +1,200 to 4,800, hiring/upskilling/retention); YTD $520M, annual $1.15B (8.5% rev), driving workload growth, 65% incident reduction, high NPS.
aspect_summary.Total revenue: actual vs. guidance, YoY: Q3 $29.8B, beating $29.0-29.5B guidance by $300M (1%), up 22% YoY (15th quarter of acceleration); other reports cite $7.8B (+28%), $22.4B (+28%), $29.2B (+32%); Q4 guide $23.8-24.2B or $30.8-31.3B (21-25%).
